Looking at this forecast, the key driver is that Apple's iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max/Ultra release date falls squarely within the target week (Sept 18, per multiple sources), following the Sept 9 announcement and Sept 11-12 pre-orders. This is historically the single largest search-interest spike in this basket, larger than the announcement itself, driven by "release date," "reviews," "unboxing," "where to buy" queries.

**1. Outside view:** Series moves ~0.3-1 pt/week typically for Tesla/Samsung/Netflix/Disney; iPhone has already been trending up (38→43 over 10 weeks) with an accelerating jump of +3.1pts in the most recent week (announcement proximity). Naive extrapolation would continue modest iPhone growth, but that undersells launch-week dynamics.

**2. Inside view:** The physical release date (Sept 18) sits inside this week — historically the peak of iPhone search interest, exceeding even the announcement week. I estimate this adds a large incremental share to iPhone, roughly +8-10pts beyond the already-elevated Sept 5 base of ~43, pushing iPhone toward ~50-53% of the basket. This mechanically compresses all other shares proportionally, since the basket is fixed-sum.

**3. Pre-mortem:** Most likely failure mode: I underestimate the iPhone spike (it could reach 55-60% if reviews/sales frenzy dominates), or overestimate it if search interest was front-loaded to the Sept 9 event week and cools by mid-September. I widen the iPhone sd substantially and keep proportional scaling for the other four, since their relative ordering (Disney > Netflix > Samsung > Tesla) has been stable.

**4. Calibration:** Widened sds relative to typical weekly moves to account for event-driven uncertainty, especially for iPhone given the unprecedented scale of the swing.
